description: Updated schema for BugSigDB microbiome study entries based on actual BugSigDB implementation. A study can contain multiple experiments, each experiment can have multiple signatures, and each signature can have multiple bacterial taxa.

hierarchy.study: Contains bibliographic information and metadata about the research paper
hierarchy.experiments: One or more experiments within the study, each representing a specific comparison between two groups
hierarchy.signatures: One or more signatures per experiment, each representing a finding of differentially abundant bacteria
hierarchy.taxa: One or more bacterial taxa per signature (all moving in the same direction)

study_id.note: Used as base page identifier in BugSigDB

pmid.note: May not always be available for preprints

uri.description: Uniform resource identifier to the paper

title.description: Full title of the research paper
title.example: Why do babies cry? Exploring the role of the gut microbiota in infantile colic, constipation, and cramps in the KOALA birth cohort study

authors.description: Comma-separated list of authors (LastName FirstInitial format)
authors.example: Smith J, Jones A, Williams B

contamination_issues_suspected.description: Contamination issues suspected in the study

results_are_suspect.description: Results are suspect for various reasons

experiments.description: One or more experiments within the study. Each experiment represents ONE comparison between TWO groups.

location_of_subjects.description: Geographic location where study subjects were recruited

host_species.description: Species from which microbiome was sampled (Latin binomial)

body_site.description: Anatomical site where microbial samples were extracted from according to the Uber Anatomy Ontology (UBERON)

condition.description: The experimental condition/phenotype studied according to the Experimental Factor Ontology (EFO) or Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO)
condition.note: The disease, phenotype, or health condition being studied

group_0_name.description: Name/label for the CONTROL (unexposed/reference) group for case-control studies
group_0_name.note: This is typically the healthy or low-symptom group

group_1_name.description: Name/label for the CASE (exposed/diseased) group for case-control studies
group_1_name.note: This is typically the diseased or high-symptom group

group_1_definition.description: Diagnostic criteria applied to define the specific condition/phenotype represented in the case (exposed) group
group_1_definition.example: High constipation: >3 days without defecation in infants <3 months. (full cohort).
group_1_definition.note: Should include specific thresholds, diagnostic tools, and inclusion criteria

group_0_definition.description: Diagnostic criteria for the control group (optional)
group_0_definition.example: Healthy controls with no GI symptoms

group_0_sample_size.description: Number of subjects in control group
group_0_sample_size.note: May not always be reported separately

group_1_sample_size.description: Number of subjects in case group
group_1_sample_size.note: May not always be reported separately

antibiotics_exclusion.description: Number of days/months without antibiotics usage and other antibiotics-related criteria used to exclude participants (if any)
antibiotics_exclusion.note: Can also be descriptive text like 'No antibiotics in past 6 months'

16s_variable_region.description: One or more hypervariable region(s) of the bacterial 16S gene

sequencing_platform.description: Manufacturer and experimental platform used for quantifying microbial abundance

data_transformation.description: Data transformation applied to microbial abundance measurements prior to differential abundance testing (if any)

statistical_test.description: Statistical method used for differential abundance testing

significance_threshold.description: p-value or FDR threshold used for differential abundance testing (if any)

mht_correction.description: Have statistical tests been corrected for multiple hypothesis testing (MHT)?
mht_correction.note: If FDR, Benjamini-Hochberg, or Bonferroni mentioned, this should be Yes

confounders_controlled_for.description: Confounding factors accounted for in statistical analysis

alpha_diversity.description: Alpha diversity metrics comparing the two groups
alpha_diversity.note: These indicate whether diversity WITHIN samples differs between groups

pielou.description: Pielou evenness index - quantifies how equal the community is numerically

interpretation.unchanged: No significant difference or not reported

shannon.description: Shannon diversity index - estimator of species richness and evenness (more weight on species richness)

interpretation.unchanged: No significant difference or not reported

inverse_simpson.description: Inverse Simpson index - modification of Simpson's index (emphasizes common species)

richness.description: Species richness - number of distinct species/taxa

interpretation.unchanged: No significant difference or not reported

chao1.description: Chao1 estimator - estimates total species richness

signatures.description: One or more signatures per experiment. Each signature represents a SET of bacteria that changed in the SAME direction.
signatures.note: Typically one signature for 'increased' bacteria and one for 'decreased' bacteria per experiment

source.description: Reference to figure/table in the paper where this signature was found

description.description: Brief description of what this signature represents (often the table/figure caption)
description.example: Results of regression models testing associations between one-month stool microbiota core genera and functional gastrointestinal symptoms.

abundance_in_group_1.description: Direction of abundance change in Group 1 (case/exposed group) with full group name
abundance_in_group_1.note: CRITICAL: All taxa in this signature moved in THIS direction

taxa.description: One or more bacterial taxa in this signature. ALL taxa in a signature have the SAME direction of change.
taxa.note: If bacteria moved in opposite directions, they belong to different signatures

ncbi_name.description: Taxonomic name of the microbe (genus, species, family, etc.)
ncbi_name.note: Should match NCBI taxonomy when possible

taxonomic_level.note: Can be inferred from the name format

quality_control.description: Quality control status for this taxon

study_to_experiments.description: One study (paper) can have many experiments (comparisons)

experiment_to_signatures.description: One experiment can have multiple signatures (typically 0-2: one for increased, one for decreased)
experiment_to_signatures.typical_range: 0-2 signatures per experiment (but can be more if multiple analyses)
experiment_to_signatures.note: Some experiments may have no significant findings (0 signatures)

signature_to_taxa.description: One signature contains multiple taxa (bacteria) that all changed in the SAME direction
signature_to_taxa.note: All taxa in a signature increased OR decreased (not mixed)

key_concepts.experiment_definition: An experiment is ONE comparison between TWO groups of subjects. Different experiments arise from: different conditions, different age groups, different statistical methods (crude vs adjusted), different subpopulations, or different timepoints.
key_concepts.signature_definition: A signature is a SET of bacteria that were significantly different in ONE experiment, all moving in the SAME DIRECTION (all increased OR all decreased in Group 1).
key_concepts.taxa_grouping: Within a signature, all taxa moved in the same direction. If Bacteria A increased and Bacteria B decreased in the same experiment, they belong to TWO DIFFERENT signatures.

common_patterns.multiple_experiments_same_condition: A single condition (e.g., colic) can have multiple experiments if analyzed with different methods (crude model vs adjusted model) or in different subpopulations (full cohort vs males only).
common_patterns.repeated_bacteria_across_experiments: The same bacteria can appear in multiple experiments across a study. This is EXPECTED and indicates consistent findings.
common_patterns.signature_splitting: If an experiment finds 10 bacteria increased and 5 bacteria decreased, this creates TWO signatures: Signature 1 (10 increased bacteria) and Signature 2 (5 decreased bacteria).

experiment_validation: Each experiment must have exactly 2 groups (Group 0 and Group 1)
Group 1 definition should be detailed and specific
Condition should map to EFO/HPO ontology
Body site should map to UBERON ontology
signature_validation: All taxa in a signature must have the same direction
Source must reference an actual table/figure
abundance_in_group_1 must match the taxa direction
taxa_validation: Taxa names should match NCBI taxonomy when possible
Scientific names should be properly formatted (italics convention)

notes: Many fields use controlled vocabularies from ontologies (UBERON, EFO, HPO)
Some fields have aliases that map to canonical terms
Quality control flags help identify potential issues with studies
Each signature represents a set of bacteria that ALL changed in the SAME direction
The same bacteria can appear in multiple experiments (this shows consistency)
Experiments are distinguished by their comparison groups, not just the condition
One paper can have 1-50+ experiments depending on the complexity of the analysis
